atoms.b: High-pitched sounds are created by ((++fast weak)) vibrations. When an object is small, tight or ((++thin plastic)), it will create a higher-pitched sound.
Low-pitched sounds are made by slower ((++vibrations instruments)). When an object is big, ((++loose square)) or thick, it will create a lower-pitched sound.

instruction.text: Select the guitar string that will make the lowest-pitched sound.

hint.text:
High-pitched sounds: small, tight or thin.
Low-pitched sounds: big, loose or thick.

instruction.text: Select the bar of the xylophone that will make the highest-pitched sound.

hint.text:
High-pitched sounds: small, tight or thin.
Low-pitched sounds: big, loose or thick.

instruction.text: Why does this bar make the highest-pitched sound?

feedback.end: The smaller, thinner or tighter something is, the higher the pitch of the sound it will make.

instruction.text: Listen to what happens to the pitch when Zoe blows across the opening of bottles 1, 2 and 3. You can repeat the sounds as many times as you need.

atoms.a: Which bottle produced the lowest-pitched sound?
Why did bottle 3 produce a lower-pitched sound?

feedback.end: Due to the bigger empty space, a lower sound was produced.

atoms.a: Will bottle 4 produce a higher or lower-pitched sound than bottle 2?

feedback.end: It will produce a lower-pitched sound since it contains more empty space.
